text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed for every task. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses labeled training data—examples that already have the correct answers. For instance, you might show it thousands of photos labeled "cat" or "dog." From these examples, the computer builds a model, which is essentially a mathematical rule that captures patterns in the data. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data, such as identifying a new photo as a cat or a dog. The accuracy of these predictions depends on the quality and amount of training data, as well as how well the model is designed. Better data and careful tuning usually lead to more reliable results.
